as_written_in_papers.quote: The c.1466_1467delTG variant—which we confirmed by capillary sequencing10 (figure 1B)—introduces a frameshift substitution of alanine for valine at position 489, generating a downstream premature stop codon (p.V489Afs*7) in the zinc finger (ZnF)2 domain of A20.
identifying a single heterozygous frameshift variant in TNFAIP3 (c.1466_1467TGdel)

cases.statement: One person: a 14-year-old boy (single case report), heterozygous, with early-onset multi-organ autoimmunity from age 10 treated with haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: insulin-dependent diabetes, cytopenias, hepatitis, enteropathy and interstitial lung disease with onset at age 10; lymphopenia with no naive T cells and a high proportion of activated T cells; refractory to immunosuppression, treated with HSCT

quotes.quote: we identified a single biologically plausible variant—a novel de novo heterozygous 2 bp deletion in tumour necrosis factor-alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3, figure 1A).

We investigated the molecular basis of complex autoimmunity—characterised by the onset of insulin-dependent diabetes, cytopaenias, hepatitis, enteropathy and interstitial lung disease at age 10—in a 14-year-old boy of healthy non-consanguineous British parents.
Immunological analysis revealed lymphopaenia with no naive T cells and a high proportion of activated T cells (table 1).
The clinical course was refractory to intensive immunosuppression with prednisolone, sirolimus, tacrolimus, infliximab or rituximab, necessitating haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The phenotype is autoimmune rather than the Behçet-like autoinflammatory picture; the authors say it expands the HA20 spectrum. STAT3 and FOXP3 variants were excluded, and exome filtering left this as the single plausible variant.

quotes.quote: Pathogenic variants in STAT3 and FOXP3 were excluded.

However, autoimmune phenomena were not prominent in a recently described cohort of patients with germline A20 haploinsufficiency, who instead presented with an autoinflammatory phenotype resembling Behçet’s disease.
This case expands the clinical spectrum of A20 haploinsufficiency.

segregation.statement: No affected relatives. The parents are described as healthy and the pedigree shows healthy unaffected siblings; the paper does not say whether the siblings were tested.

quotes.quote: The family pedigree is shown (triangles are used to preserve the anonymity of healthy unaffected siblings).

de_novo.statement: The authors call the variant de novo. The text does not describe how the parents were tested, and does not say whether parentage was confirmed (the pedigree figure is not available as text).

quotes.quote: a novel de novo heterozygous 2 bp deletion in tumour necrosis factor-alpha-induced protein 3

functional.statement: Patient dermal fibroblasts compared with controls (n=4): lower basal and TNF-induced A20 protein on immunoblot (N-terminal antibody); exaggerated and prolonged NF-κB pathway phosphorylation after TNF-α; wider and larger TNF-α-induced expression changes on RNA-seq; higher IL-6 by ELISA (p=0.0015). Inflammasome activation was not tested (no leucocyte material).

quotes.quote: V489Afs*7 reduced basal and TNF-induced A20 protein in patient (P) versus control (C1, C2) fibroblasts (immunoblot representative of n=4 independent experiments with n=4 controls).
We observed exaggerated and prolonged phosphorylation of components of the NF-κB pathway, which would be expected to enhance NF-κB-dependent transcriptional effects.

In keeping with this prediction, RNA sequencing (Illumina NextSeq-500) revealed a significant global increase in both the range and magnitude of TNF-α-stimulated differential gene expression (fold-change ≥2; false discovery rate-adjusted p≤0.01, figure 1F).
We also confirmed enhanced expression of the key NF-κB target gene interleukin 6 (IL-6) at the protein level by ELISA (p=0.0015, figure 1G).

In these respects, the molecular consequences of the p.V489Afs*7 variant were indistinguishable from reported pathogenic A20 mutations,9 although owing to the lack of leucocyte material, we were not able to extend our analysis to inflammasome activation.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Frameshift: 2-bp deletion c.1466_1467del predicted p.(Val489AlafsTer7), in the ZnF2 region per the paper. The authors describe it as loss of function.

quotes.quote: Early-onset autoimmune disease due to a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in TNFAIP3 (A20)

As A20 regulates multiple innate and adaptive signalling pathways,1 it is logical that patients with inactivating mutations in A20 might manifest pathological features of autoimmunity and/or autoinflammation.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Absent from ExAC and dbSNP, and absent from 47 unrelated disease controls, as stated by the authors.

quotes.quote: This variant is absent from public databases (ExAc/dbSNP) and distinct from disease-associated mutations affecting the ovarian tumour or ZnF4 domains of A209 (figure 1C).
genetic segregation (ie, present in patient and absent from 47 unrelated disease controls)

authors_classification.statement: No ACMG classification given. The authors call it a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation and say its molecular consequences were indistinguishable from reported pathogenic A20 mutations.

quotes.quote: Early-onset autoimmune disease due to a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in TNFAIP3 (A20)
the molecular consequences of the p.V489Afs*7 variant were indistinguishable from reported pathogenic A20 mutations

concerns: The paper states no transcript for c.1466_1467delTG; the protein it gives (p.V489Afs*7) agrees with the batch's predicted protein (protein_check: agrees).
The figure legend writes the variant as c.1466_1467TGdel, the text as c.1466_1467delTG; same deletion, different notation.
De novo status is asserted but the parental testing is not described in the text.
Single case; the patient received HSCT, so post-transplant data are not informative for the germline phenotype.
notes_for_panel: Single case report from a UK family with functional work in patient fibroblasts only. The phenotype is early-onset autoimmunity (diabetes, cytopenias, hepatitis, enteropathy, ILD) rather than Behçet-like disease.
